_comment: Docs/ingestion/rebuild-spec.md §4 — ten records over the Lonely Planet Guggenheim passage, one planted defect each, hand-read 2026-09-10 from Books/new_york/lonely-planet-new-york-city/chunk-07-upper-east-side.txt (slice 9's proof chunk may refresh them). `planted` records what a correct detector reports; under the mock client (`make ingest-calibrate`) the judged classes are scripted from it (a harness check, not a measurement); `make ingest-calibrate-live` measures.

story.title: How the museum came to be

claims.text: Solomon R. Guggenheim began collecting abstract art in his sixties, urged on by his adviser, the German baroness Hilla Rebay.
claims.span: a New York mining magnate who began acquiring abstract art in his 60s at the behest of his art adviser, an eccentric German baroness named Hilla Rebay

claims.text: Solomon Guggenheim's temporary museum, run by Hilla Rebay, opened on 54th Street in 1939 under the name Museum of Non-Objective Painting.
claims.span: In 1939, with Rebay serving as director, Guggenheim opened a temporary museum on 54th St titled the Museum of Non-Objective Painting.

claims.text: The Guggenheim building was finished in 1961, by which time both Frank Lloyd Wright and Solomon Guggenheim were dead.
claims.span: Construction was finally completed in 1959 – after both Wright and Guggenheim had passed away.

planted.reason: the span says construction was completed in 1959, not 1961

corrected.text: The Guggenheim building was finished in 1959, by which time both Frank Lloyd Wright and Solomon Guggenheim were dead.
corrected.span: Construction was finally completed in 1959 – after both Wright and Guggenheim had passed away.

records.note: The story's closing claim (completion in 1959) was deleted; the passage still states it.
